_comment: One table of capture-window cases, read by BOTH suites, so the app has one
way of saying *when a picture was shot*.
Four surfaces render a stack's capture window, and they used to be four
implementations of three slightly different rules: `formatCaptureNights` in
`frontend/src/format.ts` (every screen), `format_acq_range` in
`seestack/nameplate.py` (the caption baked onto a shared JPEG),
`_format_night_range` in `seestack/imaging_log.py` (the exported spreadsheet)
and — since v0.328.3 — the Editor's copyable caption. All four read the same
two ISO dates off the same run, so a beginner comparing the picture on screen
with the caption they copied and the log row they exported saw one night
spelled three ways.
The three *styles* are deliberate and stay: `ascii` because the bundled
nameplate font has no en dash, `iso` because a spreadsheet cell must stay
sortable and must not read as arithmetic. The rest of the rule — write the
shared parts once, space the dash only between multi-word sides, print a
reversed window forwards — is `seestack/nightrange.py`, once.
Readers: tests/test_nightrange.py (all three styles) and
frontend/src/format.test.ts (the `display` style, against
`formatCaptureNights`). A change to either side that isn't a change to the
other now reddens a suite.
Each case is [start, end, {style: expected}]. `null` means the app never
recorded that end.
